Compute Coefficient of Variation (CV)

Source: R/cv.R
cv.Rd

This function calculates the coefficient of variation (CV), which is a standardized measure of dispersion, defined as the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean.

Usage

cv(x, na_rm = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector.

na_rm

A logical value indicating whether to remove NA values before computation. Default is TRUE.

Value

A numeric value representing the coefficient of variation. If x contains only NA values or has a mean of zero, the function returns NA_real_.

Details

The ratio is meaningful only on a scale with a true zero. For temperatures, use kelvin: in Celsius or Fahrenheit the same series gives different values, and a mean near zero inflates the ratio without bound. calc_par() converts C and F to kelvin for this statistic by itself.

Examples

x <- c(10, 15, 20, 25, 30)
cv(x)  # Compute CV for a numeric vector
#> [1] 0.3952847

x_with_na <- c(10, 15, NA, 25, 30)
cv(x_with_na)  # Removes NA by default
#> [1] 0.4564355
cv(x_with_na, na_rm = FALSE)  # Returns NA if missing values exist
#> [1] NA

x_zero_mean <- c(-5, 5, -5, 5)
cv(x_zero_mean)  # Returns NA since mean is zero
#> [1] NA
